transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A dishwasher tripping the mains (RCD/fuse) intermittently is a safety issue. Because this involves live electricity and water, you must stop using the appliance until we have identified the cause; repeated tripping can damage the wiring or create a shock hazard. The most common cause for a trip occurring around 15 minutes into a cycle is a failing heater element. As the element gets hot, insulation breakdowns can allow electricity to 'leak' to earth (the metal casing), which trips your safety switch. Other possibilities include a leaking circulation pump or a chafed wire in the door hinge area that shorts out when the machine vibrates. Does it happen right as the heating phase begins (usually after the initial wash/rinse)?
2. Or does it happen while the machine is just circulating water (washing) before any significant heating?
3. Or is it truly random within that time frame? Please let me know which of those fits best, and we can decide on the next safe step.

I can't tell exactly when the heating starts, sorry. It's only happened on the 65C programme, somewhere between 10 and 20 mins in, so not the same minute each time. The quick cold rinse has never tripped it. It takes out a whole bank of circuits including the fridge, which is why I'm a bit worried. No burning smell though.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The most common culprit is the heater element itself: over time, the insulation inside its metal tube can degrade, allowing electricity to 'leak' to the casing when it gets hot, which trips your RCD. To confirm this safely (with the machine unplugged), please remove the lower kickplate/grille at the bottom front. Look at the heater element (a metal loop or bar). If you see any cracks, burns, or pitting on the metal surface, that is likely the cause. Please describe exactly what condition it is in.

Sorry, I'm not comfortable taking the kickplate or any covers off, it's mains electrics and water. I can tell you the floor and socket are dry and there's no visible leak or damage. Is there anything else I can check from the outside, or should I get an engineer in?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
There is nothing safe you can check from the outside that will confirm or rule out an internal electrical fault like this. Because the appliance is tripping your RCD (the device that cuts power to protect against shock) and it affects other circuits, you must not use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Tiny cracks allow current to 'leak' to the earth (the casing), which trips your safety switch. It can be intermittent because the expansion of the metal when hot changes how the leak behaves. Please arrange for a qualified appliance engineer or electrician to attend. They will need to isolate the machine and test the resistance of the heater element and other live components to find the source of the earth leakage. Do not attempt to bypass the RCD or force it to stay on; that is dangerous.
